name: Ivory Remnant

stars.name: Ivory
stars.notes: Cooling white dwarf, remnant of a star that exhausted its fuel billions of years ago, faint but still radiating stored thermal energy

planets.name: Cinder
planets.notes: Stripped planetary core, atmosphere long since blown away during the star's red giant phase

planets.name: The Ossuary
planets.notes: Dead world bearing unmistakable signs of ancient habitation—geometric surface formations visible from orbit, origin unknown

planets.name: Pallor
planets.notes: Dense rocky world with a faint residual magnetic field, surface covered in crystallized silicate formations from rapid cooling

planets.name: Shroud
planets.notes: Massive ice world that likely migrated inward after the star's collapse, may preserve pre-collapse material in deep ice layers

anomalies.name: The Whisper Field
anomalies.notes: Low-frequency electromagnetic emissions centered on The Ossuary's geometric formations, structured but undeciphered, intensify during planetary conjunction

asteroid_belts.name: Bone Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: Debris from worlds destroyed during the star's red giant expansion, contains fragments of planetary crust and mantle material

stations.name: Remembrance Station
stations.notes: Archaeological research station studying the geometric surface formations, jointly funded by three universities

stations.name: Lantern Post
stations.notes: White dwarf observation platform studying stellar cooling curves and remnant physics

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed system under academic research charter, access governed by the Tri-University Archaeological Compact

history: Cataloged in 2267 as part of a white dwarf census, the system attracted no attention until 2544 when a survey vessel detected the geometric formations on The Ossuary.

The Tri-University Archaeological Compact established Remembrance Station in 2551, and three decades of study have confirmed the formations are artificial but failed to identify their creators or purpose.

Detection of the Whisper Field in 2603 added urgency to research; the structured electromagnetic emissions suggest the formations may still be active in some capacity, billions of years after the civilization that built them presumably perished.
description: Ivory Remnant is a tomb. The white dwarf at its center is the pale corpse of a star that burned through its fuel billions of years before humanity learned to make fire, and its retinue of dead worlds orbit in silence through the faint blue-white glow that remains. Four planets survived the star's death throes in various states of ruin—stripped cores, frozen husks, and surfaces reshaped by the violence of a red giant's expansion. The system is cold, dim, and profoundly still.

What draws the living to this dead place is The Ossuary. The second planet bears geometric formations spanning hundreds of kilometers—precise lines, repeated angles, structures that no natural process could produce. Someone built here, long ago, when Ivory was a living star and The Ossuary may have been a habitable world. Remembrance Station's researchers have mapped the formations exhaustively but cannot agree on what they were for. The leading theories range from a planetary-scale computing architecture to a religious monument to something that has no analogue in human experience.

The Whisper Field changed everything. When researchers detected structured electromagnetic emissions emanating from the formations, the implications were staggering: whatever was built on The Ossuary may still be functioning, powered by an energy source that has survived a stellar death. The signals intensify during rare alignments of the remaining planets, suggesting the entire system may have been engineered as a single instrument. What it measures, or what it communicates with, is the question that haunts every researcher on Remembrance Station—and the reason the Compact has quietly begun restricting information about what their instruments have recorded.
